title: Steamships and ocean steam navigation
summary: On 17 August 1807 Robert Fulton's North River steamboat left New York City and reached Albany, 150 miles up the Hudson, in about 32 hours: the first commercially successful steamboat. Steam river boats soon transformed American transport. At sea, the Great Western Steamship Company's SS Great Western opened a transatlantic service in 1838, and its SS Great Britain, the first large ocean-going ship to combine an iron hull with a screw propeller, crossed the Atlantic in 14 days in 1845.

uncertainty.note: From Fulton's first Hudson run (17 August 1807) to the first Atlantic crossing by an iron screw steamer (1845).
